web_blocks.html: GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF (NASDAQ: NBIL) uses total return swaps to seek 200% of the daily return of Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ: NBIS), charging a 1.41% fee on $130.88 million in AUM [1][2][18]. On November 13, 2026, NBIL closed at $4.95 (-19.77% on 32.95M shares, 3.07x 30-day average volume), down -92.77% from its $68.49 peak and -58.26% over one year (Finviz: -61.48%) [1][38]. NBIL is graded FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL (underlying KPIs PASS_WITH_WATCH) and REJECTED for all new equity or options capital [38]. For our existing 50.0-share Robinhood holding ($247.50 value, -$769.95 unrealized loss), the required action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY [38].

The thesis rests on a two-layer failure. First, NBIL's daily-reset swap wrapper imposes a quadratic volatility tax of -σ² each year [5]. At NBIS's ~100% realized volatility regime, NBIL loses over 63% per year even if NBIS finishes flat [5]. Second, Nebius Group's AI cloud demand is real ($38.7B RPO, $6.4B Q3 2026 ARR, $980.8M Q3 revenue, +571% YoY) [39]. Yet management's November 12 Q3 release raised FY2026 CapEx to ~$27 billion and FY2027 CapEx to $40B–$45B atop $14.19B in carrying debt [24][35][39]. Free cash flow stays deeply negative (-$3.66B in FY2025) [31]. Both NBIS ($115.88, 14.38x P/S) and NBIL ($4.95, 78.95% below its $23.52 200-day SMA) sit in entrenched Weinstein Stage 4 downtrends [38][40].

book_paragraphs: This monograph evaluates GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF (NASDAQ: NBIL) as of the November 13, 2026 market close ($4.95, down 19.77% on 32.95 million shares). Our conclusion is unequivocal: NBIL fails fundamental compounding standards (FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL), is REJECTED for any new equity or options capital across short-, medium-, and long-term horizons, and carries an immediate EXIT_IMMEDIATELY directive on the portfolio's 50.0 shares held in Robinhood.

Why is the verdict so decisive? Because NBIL traps investors inside two compounding risks at once. On the wrapper layer, a 2x daily-reset ETF rebalances its swap exposure every afternoon at 4:00 PM ET, creating a continuous mathematical drag equal to minus one times the underlying stock's annualized variance. In a 100% volatility regime—typical for a hyper-capex AI infrastructure stock—NBIL forfeits more than 60% of its net asset value over twelve months even if the underlying equity goes nowhere.

On the operating layer, Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS) is scaling rapidly—posting $980.8 million in Q3 2026 revenue (+571% YoY) and $38.7 billion in backlog anchored by Microsoft and Meta—yet its capital intensity has escalated beyond self-funding limits. With FY2026 CapEx raised to ~$27 billion, FY2027 CapEx guided to $40B–$45B, and $14.19 billion in carrying debt already on the balance sheet, both NBIS ($115.88, 14.38x sales) and NBIL ($4.95, 78.95% below its 200-day moving average) have broken into Weinstein Stage 4 downtrends.

Rather than anchoring on our -$769.95 unrealized loss (-75.67% vs. $20.35 cost basis), disciplined capital management requires liquidating all 50 shares (~$247.50 proceeds) and redeploying 50% into Stage 2 compounder Microsoft (MSFT) and 50% into Cash Reserve.

Notice how this decision separates two ideas that investors often confuse: admiring a company's top-line growth versus owning a flawed financial instrument. Nebius Group has genuine engineering talent, strategic backing from NVIDIA, and massive hyperscaler contracts. Yet admiring Nebius Group's revenue growth is no reason to hold a 2x daily-reset derivative wrapper in a Stage 4 downtrend while the underlying business burns tens of billions of dollars in capital expenditures. Great portfolio management is not about finding excuses to hold onto losing positions; it is about ruthlessly rotating capital out of negative-expectancy vehicles and into asymmetric Stage 2 compounders.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Monograph
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 dissect NBIL's 1940 Act swap mechanics alongside Nebius Group's business model, hyperscaler contracts, balance-sheet leverage, and management governance. Chapters 7 through 9 then translate those facts into a Reverse DCF of NBIS, a mathematical volatility-decay matrix, a multi-timeframe Stage 4 tape and options audit, and our binding EXIT_IMMEDIATELY and capital-redeployment plan.

Even though our Robinhood position represents just 0.28% of total portfolio net worth ($247.50 out of $88,684.68), portfolio discipline is indivisible. Eliminating dead-weight leveraged ETFs, harvesting the -$769.95 tax loss, and rotating half into a Stage 2 institutional compounder (MSFT) and half into cash strengthens overall portfolio quality and lowers portfolio beta.

Every section of this monograph is anchored to the verified November 13, 2026 market-session close and Nebius Group's November 12, 2026 third-quarter financial release. Readers will see why Nebius Group's rapid revenue acceleration—reaching $980.8 million in Q3 2026 with $38.7 billion in remaining performance obligations—cannot rescue a 2x daily-reset ETF when capital expenditures surge to $27 billion in FY2026 and $40 billion to $45 billion in FY2027. When an underlying equity enters a high-volatility Stage 4 correction, daily rebalancing acts as a silent tax that locks in losses on every bounce and sell-off. Our mandate is clear: exit all 50 shares immediately, deploy zero new equity or options capital into NBIL, and put the recovered cash to work in higher-quality opportunities.

Think of this prologue as your pre-flight checklist before diving into the ten-chapter deep dive. In Chapters 1 through 3, we unpack the two-layer architecture of NBIL and trace how Nebius Group emerged from the $5.4 billion Yandex N.V. carve-out to sign landmark multi-year GPU contracts with Microsoft and Meta. In Chapters 4 through 6, we audit the competitive moat against hyperscalers and neocloud peers, scrutinize management's capital-allocation track record, and dissect the balance-sheet transformation from net cash to $14.19 billion of carrying debt. Finally, Chapters 7 through 9 deliver the Reverse DCF math, the multi-timeframe tape and options liquidity audit, and the exact execution steps to exit NBIL and redeploy into Microsoft and cash.
